body: More than half of conflict deaths since 1989 have occurred in Africa

The first bar shows that globally, an estimated 3.9 million people — combatants and civilians — died due to fighting in armed conflicts between 1989 (the first year for which data is available) and 2024.
This number comes from the Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP), which uses news reports, other contemporary sources, and academic research to count the deaths in armed conflicts worldwide.1
The data does not include deaths due to disease and starvation resulting from conflicts, which can make the death toll much larger.

The Middle East and Asia were the next most affected regions
Europe and the Americas saw the fewest deaths, with around 370,000 and 230,000 deaths, respectively.
